facts.raw_span: A ten-month-old Hispanic girl presented for evaluation of facial asymmetry noted since birth
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
Pregnancy was uncomplicated, and the patient was born full term
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
her face is symmetric at rest
When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward
frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides
A neurodevelopmental examination is normal
Magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals is normal
echocardiography shows no cardiac anomalies
an auditory brainstem response test reveals normal hearing pathways

concepts.why: The patient's facial asymmetry noted since birth, with the right lower lip deviating inward when smiling, suggests a congenital condition.
The patient's abnormal lip movement and symmetric facial movement at rest are consistent with Moebius Syndrome, a congenital disorder affecting the cranial nerves.
The patient's right lower lip deviating inward when smiling suggests a unilateral congenital lower lip palsy.
The patient's abnormal facial movement, with the right lower lip deviating inward, is consistent with facial hemiparesis, a condition affecting the cranial nerves.
The patient's normal developmental milestones, uncomplicated pregnancy, and normal neurodevelopmental examination suggest a normal variant or anatomical variation.

concepts.preferred_label: Benign Congenital Hypertrophy of the Lower Lip
concepts.why: The patient's right lower lip deviating inward when smiling may be due to a benign congenital hypertrophy of the lower lip.
The patient's facial asymmetry when crying, with the right lower lip deviating inward, is consistent with asymmetric crying face syndrome.
The patient's right lower lip deviating inward when smiling suggests a congenital lower lip paresis.
The inward deviation of the right lower lip when smiling or crying, despite normal imaging and auditory tests, suggests a specific diagnosable entity of Congenital Unilateral Lower Lip Palsy.
